mechanism: Transform the {{problem}} statement by changing perspective, scope, or framing. This mechanism not only restructures the current solver tree but actively seeks a new solver root better aligned with the transformed problem. Techniques: invert the goal, change the subject, shift time horizon, alter constraints. A problem unsolvable in frame A may be trivial in frame B.
gloss: Changing perspective to restructure the tree and find a new solution root
failure_modes: Frame Blindness: New frame has its own blind spots, trading one bias for another.
invariants: Retains the original {{problem}} statement alongside the transformed one.
Names which transformation was applied — inverting the goal, changing the subject, shifting the horizon, altering constraints.
